I want to include more options when setting alerts in Datadog. I can suggest using "Group by" tags for better organization and enabling "Notify no data as OK" to avoid false alerts. Additionally, I should set "Automatic recovery when the metric hasn't increased for a specified number of minutes." Goal: alert only when a new OOM termination happens, not when the container keeps the last_state.terminated flag set after restart. Solution approach (UI-only): build a metric monitor that looks for an increase in the kubernetes.containers.last_state.terminated metric (i.e., a new transition), rather than monitoring the absolute value. Then pick an evaluation window/rollup so the monitor sees new occurrences but will recover once there are no new increases.

Step-by-step in the Datadog web UI

1. Open the Datadog app and go to Monitors > New Monitor.
2. Choose “Metric” as the monitor type.
3. Select the metric kubernetes.containers.last_state.terminated from the metric picker.
4. Scope the monitor to the relevant cluster/namespaces/pods/tags so you only get alerts for the containers you care about (use the scope box to add node, cluster, namespace, deployment, pod, container, or any other tags).
5. In the “Alert Conditions” section, change how the metric is evaluated: switch from evaluating the raw value to evaluating changes over time. In the UI this is done by selecting the “Alert on” mode that detects increases (look for the option named like “Alert on: change / increase” or “Alert on: rise”).
   - Choose to alert when the metric increases by at least 1 (i.e., a new terminated state observed).
   - Set the timeframe to a short rolling window that makes sense for your environment (for example: evaluate increases over the last 5 minutes). This ensures a single OOM produces a detected increase and a timely alert.
6. Configure the rollup/aggregation: use a rollup that counts or sums occurrences over the chosen timeframe (UI option often shown as “rollup” or “over X minutes”). This makes the monitor detect new events rather than sticky values.
7. Set the evaluation timing / recovery behavior:
   - Pick an evaluation window that lets the monitor recover once there are no new increases for a period (for example, “alert if increase seen in the last 5 minutes; recover if no increase for X minutes”).
   - If available, enable the option to “Alert when the change is detected” rather than alerting while the value remains 1.
8. Choose how to handle missing data: set “Missing data” / “No data” to be OK (so the monitor won’t stay in alert because of absent points).
9. Configure the notification message, tags to include (pod, namespace, node), and who to notify.
10. (Optional) Add a runbook link describing how to inspect the pod/container and confirm an OOM.
11. Save the monitor.

Why this works (briefly): you’re detecting increases in the metric (new terminated states) rather than the metric’s absolute value. When the container restarts and the metric stays reported as 1, there is no new increase so the monitor won’t re-alert and can recover after the configured window with no further increases.

Tuning tips
- If you get noisy alerts from restarts that aren’t OOMs, tighten the scope (add tags) or increase the required increase threshold or add a small cooldown window.
- If you want one alert per pod/container instance, group by the pod/container tag in the monitor so each entity has its own alerting evaluation.
- Test with a short evaluation window first, then lengthen to reduce noise.

If you want, I can walk through the exact UI labels for your Datadog account version (some wording differs slightly across Datadog releases).
